extracted.intended_audience: general readers and people interested in television/screenwriting (fans, students, writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Dan Harmon's 'story circle' — an adaptation of the hero's journey into an eight-step circular process for writing coherent stories for television and film. Useful as a prescriptive technique for screenwriters to structure plots and character arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story circle technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmon adapted the hero's journey into a circular eight-step process he calls the 'story circle'. The circle is divided into eight segments, each representing a stage of the plot. He writes the steps as follows: 'A character is in a zone of comfort or familiarity. They desire something. They enter an unfamiliar situation. They adapt to that situation. They get that which they wanted. They pay a heavy price for it. They return to their familiar situation. They have changed as a result of the journey.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended as a simplified, reliable structure to produce coherent stories; Harmon uses it whenever writing and claims 'I can't not see that circle. It's tattooed on my brain.' He argues the circle 'can supposedly be applied to all stories' and has used it extensively in Community and Rick and Morty. He contrasts film and television aims: 'A feature film's job is to send you out of the theatre on a high in 90 minutes. Television's job is to keep you glued to the television for your entire life... It just means that the focus of step 8 is less riling-things-up and more getting-things-back-to-where-they-started.' In a blog post detailing the second sector he explains its purpose: the protagonist is 'thrown into the water and now it's sink or swim... There's no room for bullshit in the unconscious basement.' The page presents the story circle as both a prescriptive checklist of eight narrative stages and a flexible framework with different emphases for film versus television; examples and applications include Harmon's work on Community and Rick and Morty.
